welcomeEmail.name: Welcome Email (New Patient Referral)
welcomeEmail.subject: Welcome to Mount Sinai Fertility – Referral Received
welcomeEmail.body:
Hello,

We have received your referral from your referring physician or nurse practitioner. Before we can process it, please confirm the information below to ensure your file is accurate and complete.

1. Please confirm your email address – Kindly reply to confirm that this is the correct email for you.

2. Your personal information – Please provide the following:

  • Complete Last, First Name:
  • Date of Birth (MM/DD/YYYY):
  • Address (include unit number, if applicable):
  • Phone Number:
  • Email:
  • Ontario Health Card Number + Version Code (up to date):

If you do NOT have OHIP – Please attach:

  • Valid government photo ID (Passport or Driver's Licence)
  • Out-of-province health card (if applicable)

Please note: Out-of-province patients will be subject to fees. These will be reviewed with you by the MD admin when scheduling your appointment.

If you have UHIP – Please attach:

  • A copy of your UHIP card
  • A government photo ID

3. Partner information (if applicable) – If you have a partner, please provide the following. If you do not have a partner, kindly indicate this.

  • Complete Last, First Name:
  • Date of Birth (MM/DD/YYYY):
  • Address (include unit number, if applicable):
  • Phone Number:
  • Email:
  • Ontario Health Card Number + Version Code:

If your partner does NOT have OHIP – Please attach:

  • Valid government photo ID
  • Out-of-province health card (if applicable)

Note: Out-of-province fees apply as above.

4. Emergency contact information – As per hospital policy, we require emergency contact information for you (and your partner, if applicable). If your partner will be your emergency contact, simply indicate this, and you do not need to complete the section below.

Patient Emergency Contact

  • Relationship to Patient:
  • Last, First Name:
  • Phone Number:
  • Address (include unit number if applicable):

Partner Emergency Contact (if applicable)

  • Relationship to Patient:
  • Last, First Name:
  • Phone Number:
  • Address (include unit number if applicable):

Next steps – Once we receive the above information, your referral will be processed and forwarded to one of our MD administrative coordinators. They will contact you directly to schedule your appointment.

Thank you for taking the time to provide this information,
{{signature}}

1. Kindly confirm that this is your correct email.

Thank you,

eefAgeOver40Patient.name: EEF Patient Age > 40 (Patient Letter)
eefAgeOver40Patient.subject: Mount Sinai Fertility – Egg Freezing Age Information
eefAgeOver40Patient.body:
Dear Patient,

We received your referral from your physician for self-pay egg freezing.

At our centre, we do not offer elective egg freezing after the age of 40. This is because the number and health of the eggs in the ovaries decrease over time and the success rates for assisted reproductive technologies declines with age.

We do offer other options for building a family and would be happy to discuss these with you.

Sincerely,

Mount Sinai Fertility Referral Coordinator

T: 416-586-4800 x 2778
F: 416-586-4686

araPatient.name: ARA Patient (Patient Letter)
araPatient.subject: Mount Sinai Fertility – Fertility Treatment Options
araPatient.body:
Dear Patient,

We received your referral from your physician for fertility.

At our centre, we do not recommend fertility treatments such as in-vitro fertilization after the age of 43. This is because the number and health of the eggs in the ovaries decrease over time and the success rates for assisted reproductive technologies is extremely low after the age of 43. We have included an information sheet on reproductive aging and ovarian function.

We do offer other options for building a family such as the use of eggs from a donor and would be happy to discuss these with you. If you are interested in discussing these options, your physician can let us know we should proceed with the referral and consultation.

Sincerely,

Mount Sinai Fertility Referral Coordinator

T: 416-586-4800 x 2778
F: 416-586-4686

REPRODUCTIVE AGING AND OVARIAN FUNCTION

Your reproductive system ages faster than you may realize. Some people, once ready to conceive, find that they have problems getting pregnant due to age-related infertility. Other people are surprised when they begin developing symptoms of menopause, such as hot flashes, while they still feel young and healthy. Understanding the stages your reproductive system goes through is important in understanding these changes in your body.

What are the stages of reproduction?

Reproductive Years
The first menstrual period occurs around age 12. Periods (cycles) may be irregular at first but should become regular over the next few years. Contraception is needed if a person is sexually active with a person with sperm and does not want to become pregnant. Fertility peaks from the late teens through the late 20s and then begins to decline. By age 30, the chance of miscarriage begins to increase, and the chance of becoming pregnant starts to decrease.

Menopausal Transition
Usually in one's 40s, a person will begin the transition from reproductive years to menopause. The length of menstrual cycles will start to vary, and they may begin to skip periods. They may experience hot flashes due to decreased estrogen production by the ovaries and may have difficulty sleeping. The average age of the final menstrual period (menopause) is age 51.

Post-menopause
After menopause, pregnancy is no longer possible. Ovaries produce very little estrogen, which results in vaginal dryness and bone loss. Hot flashes intensify and then begin to subside. Hormone therapy or other treatments may be appropriate for short-term use.

How does reproductive aging affect fertility?
By age 40, many people will not be able to have a successful pregnancy. By age 45, very few people will be able to have a successful pregnancy. This happens because both the quality and quantity of eggs remaining in your ovaries gradually declines throughout your life, and this decline accelerates beginning around age 35. Age is the best indicator of egg quality. The decreasing quantity of eggs in the ovaries is called "loss of ovarian reserve." People begin to lose ovarian reserve before they become infertile and before they stop having regular periods. There are medical tests for ovarian reserve. These tests do not indicate whether pregnancy is possible but can give information about whether age-related changes of the ovaries have begun. People with poor ovarian reserve have a lower chance of becoming pregnant than people with expected ovarian reserve in their same age group.

What are my options?
People who wish to delay childbearing until their late 30s or early 40s may consider methods of fertility preservation such as egg retrieval either followed by freezing of the eggs or in vitro fertilization (IVF) followed by freezing of the embryos. The success of embryo freezing is well established, but it requires that the person have a partner with sperm or use donor sperm. With egg freezing, a partner or sperm source is not needed at the time or for future decisions, but it is a newer procedure. The only option for people who already have infertility due to age is to use eggs or embryos donated by a younger person. This option can provide high chances for pregnancy even when there has been a loss of ovarian reserve or function.

Adapted from: "Reproductive Aging in Women". American Society for Reproductive Medicine (ASRM) Fact Sheet.

We currently only offer elective egg freezing to patients who are 40 or younger due to the age-related decline in ovarian function as egg quantity and quality both decline dramatically with age.

eefPedsPhysician.name: EEF Patient Age < 18
eefPedsPhysician.body:
{{currentDate}}

Dear Dr. {{referringPhysician}},

Patient: {{patientName}}                    HC: {{patientHC}}

We received your recent referral for a patient for egg freezing. At this time, we are not offering egg freezing for individuals less than 18 years of age for several reasons. There can be increased difficulty performing the required vaginal procedures as well as potential sedation concerns in individuals less than 18 years of age. In addition, disposition options are more limited for gametes retrieved before age 18 (i.e. gametes can only be used for individual's own use and cannot be left to a future partner). In addition, aneuploidy rates in eggs are higher during adolescence than in mid-twenties.

We recommend that patients who are less than 18 proceed with egg freezing at a later stage. Patients do not need to delay starting on testosterone treatment until after egg freezing is complete as egg freezing can be done in the future with 2 week to 3 month period of discontinuation of testosterone therapy before stimulation or testosterone therapy may be continued during stimulation.

We will contact your patient and will counsel them regarding the above information and recommend that they proceed with egg freezing at a later stage. While we appreciate and welcome referrals for discussion of egg freezing, please consider deferring future referrals until after patients have turned 18.

Sincerely,

Kimberly Liu, MD, FRCSC, MSL
Medical Director, Mount Sinai Fertility

araPhysician.name: ARA Patient
araPhysician.body:
{{currentDate}}

Dear Dr. {{referringPhysician}},

Re: {{patientName}}                    HC: {{patientHC}}

We received your referral for the above-named patient for fertility. Prior to accepting this referral, we feel it is important to inform you that your patient exceeds our recommended age limit for some of our fertility treatment options.

We currently only recommend fertility treatments such as in-vitro fertilization to patients who are younger than 43 years of age due to the age-related decline in ovarian function as egg quantity and quality both decline dramatically after the age of 40. Only patients who are under 43 can access funding for IVF from the Ontario Fertility Program. In addition, the live birth rates using assisted reproductive technologies are very low for those greater than age 43.

We would be happy to see your patient to discuss fertility options such as egg donation which would offer the best chance for pregnancy.

We ask that you convey this information to your patient. We have also provided a patient information letter below if you would like to share this with your patient. If your patient would still like to proceed with a referral, please resend a referral letter with this updated information.

Sincerely,

{{signature}} Referral Coordinator

spermBanking.body:
{{currentDate}}

Dear Dr. {{referringPhysician}},

Re: {{patientName}}                    HC: {{patientHC}}

Mount Sinai Fertility has received this referral and would like to confirm whether the patient has any medical indication or an upcoming procedure that may impact fertility.

At present, our clinic offers sperm banking services only for patients with oncology diagnoses, those undergoing hormone replacement therapy (HRT), or individuals with other medical conditions or planned surgical interventions that may affect fertility. We do not offer sperm banking for non-medical or lifestyle purposes.

If the referral is for non-medical sperm banking, we kindly suggest redirecting the patient to ReproMed for further assistance.

Thank you for your understanding.

Sincerely,

Abena Kyereh-Darkwah
Referrals Coordinator

iudInsertion.name: IUD Insertion
iudInsertion.body:
{{currentDate}}

Dear Dr. {{referringPhysician}},

Re: {{patientName}}                    HC: {{patientHC}}

Mount Sinai Fertility has received this referral; however, we are unable to accept it.

Our physicians do not recommend performing intrauterine device (IUD) insertion at the time of oocyte retrieval (OPU), particularly in cases where a difficult insertion is anticipated. The level of sedation provided during OPU is not sufficient for this type of procedure, and such interventions are not performed at our clinic.

We kindly recommend that the patient be referred to a general gynecologist for IUD insertion in a formal operating room setting, with ultrasound guidance as appropriate.

Thank you for your understanding.

Sincerely,

Abena Kyereh-Darkwah
Referrals Coordinator
